title: The Accurate map of the coast
subtitle: 科学探索 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 科学探索（科学与技术·科学精神、科学探究）
meta: 主题语境：科学探索（科学与技术·科学精神、科学探究）　|　核心词汇：accurate　|　正文 340 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 accurate 的用法与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1972 the driver wrote of ① an accurate map of the coast in the timetable, and everybody in the station said at once that it was ② more accurate than the one named there the year before. Three days on, people still spoke of that morning, and of how the driver, who never explained anything, had done it in silence and gone home; it was the accurate ones, my mother said, that people remembered longest.

It was ③ the most accurate map of the coast anybody in the station had ever seen, or so the timetable for February 1966 claims. My mother, who had seen them all, thought it ④ too accurate to be of any use to anybody, and said as much to the passenger who had come to help; the accurate ones, she used to say, were never the useful ones.

My uncle, who kept the ticket at the far platform, meant something else entirely. He called the whole business ⑤ an accurate account of that night, and said that no passenger in his right mind would call it ⑥ as accurate as the account of that night they had once had in the old station. He was never a man who cared whether a thing was accurate or not, and he said so.

By 1979 the matter had shrunk to half a line in the timetable. What the line asked for was ⑦ something accurate, and nothing besides. The passenger from the next station called the whole plan ⑧ quite accurate; everybody laughed, and then did exactly what he had said. After that the timetable kept the names of the accurate ones only.

My mother said nothing at all. In 1982, twice over, she wrote of another accurate map of the coast in the same timetable, and the work, which took two days, seemed  more accurate than anybody had expected.  The most accurate account of that night in the whole station, she said in 1984, was the one she could never quite name; the accurate ones, she added, are always the ones that stay.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. adj. 准确（前置定语 an accurate map of the coast：1972 年司机在时刻表里记下的那件准确的海岸图）
B. adj. 准确／精密（比较级 more accurate than：文中两处，一处比海岸图，一处比预想）
C. adj. 准确／精密（最高级 the most accurate：文中两处，见第 3、10 题）
D. adj. 准确（表语 too accurate to do：母亲觉得它太准确，反倒派不上用场）
E. adj. 精密（前置定语 an accurate account of that night：叔叔把整件事称作一桩精密的记述）
F. adj. 精密（同级比较 as accurate as：拿眼前这桩跟旧日那桩那晚的记述相比）
G. adj. 精密（后置定语 something accurate：修饰不定代词时须放在其后）
H. adj. 精密（受程度副词修饰 quite accurate：那位乘客的评价）

items.q: an accurate map of the coast
the most accurate map of the coast anybody
an accurate account of that night

answers.why: accurate 意为“准确”，1972 年司机在时刻表里记下的是“一件准确的海岸图”，此处作前置定语 an accurate map of the coast。
accurate 意为“准确”，此处用比较级 more accurate than，拿它跟前一年记下的那一个相比。
accurate 意为“准确”，时刻表上 二月 那行字说它是车站里最准确的一件，故用最高级 the most accurate map of the coast。
accurate 意为“准确”，母亲认为这件东西“太准确了，谁也用不上”，too accurate to do 表示“太……以致不能”。
accurate 意为“精密”，叔叔把整件事称作“一桩精密的记述”，此处作前置定语 an accurate account of that night。
accurate 意为“精密”，叔叔不肯说它“跟旧日那桩那晚的记述一样精密”，同级比较用 as accurate as。
accurate 意为“精密”，时刻表上那半行字要的是“精密的东西”，something 被形容词修饰时形容词须后置：something accurate。
accurate 意为“精密”，邻车站来的那位乘客认为这套计划“相当精密”，quite 修饰原级 accurate。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1972 年，司机在时刻表里记下了一件准确的海岸图。（an accurate map of the coast）
人人都说它比前一年记下的那一个更准确。（more accurate than …）

他说，谁也不会认为它跟旧日那桩那晚的记述一样精密。（as accurate as …）
到了 1979 年，时刻表上只剩半行字：要的是一件精密的东西。（something accurate）
answers: In 1972 the driver wrote of an accurate map of the coast in the timetable.
Everybody said it was more accurate than the one named there the year before.
My mother thought it too accurate to be of any use to anybody.
My uncle called the whole business an accurate account of that night.
He said nobody would call it as accurate as the account of that night they had once had.

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作

answers: In 1972 the driver wrote of an accurate map of the coast in the timetable, and nobody forgot it.
It was the most accurate map of the coast in the station, or so the timetable says.
My mother thought it too accurate to be of any use, and said so plainly.
